nodes.name: Compound crystal wafer substrates (GaN, GaAs, InP, SiC)
nodes.description: Raw feedstock tier of compound/wide-bandgap semiconductor wafers for specialty analog and power device fabrication. Includes GaAs/InP single-crystal wafers for optical communications and RF devices; GaN-on-SiC and SiC crystal wafers for power semiconductor manufacturing. This referent is distinct from silicon-wafer feedstock and carries its own concentrated merchant supplier base (Wolfspeed, Sumitomo, AXT, Freiberger, IntelliEPI). Maturity: GaAs/InP mature commodity for 20+ years; SiC transitioning from 6-inch to 8-inch production (2024-2026); GaN-on-SiC nascent and geopolitically exposed to China gallium controls.

nodes.notes: Referent: compound/specialty crystal wafer substrates for power and optical semiconductor manufacturing (silicon independent). SiC substrate market shifted from severe shortage (2022, ~1 year lead time) to oversupply (2024-2025) due to Chinese capacity expansions; current phase: 8-inch ramp and 14-inch research (China 2026) redrawing capacity landscape. GaAs/InP remain stable commodity. InP optical substrate emerging as new bottleneck for AI datacenter 1.6T/800G transceivers; Coherent and NVIDIA securing multi-year LTAs through 2030; China export controls (gallium, indium) create geopolitical exposure. Not a current bottleneck for HBM CoWoS-class AI accelerator modules but critical upstream tier for power-delivery specialty devices in the broader AI platform (power delivery, cooling, optical interconnect).

nodes.name: Epitaxial layer growth services and MOCVD/MBE materials
nodes.description: Specialty materials tier: semiconductor epitaxial growth (MOCVD, MBE) for compound devices (GaAs/InP optical and RF devices; GaN power devices). Supplied by dedicated epitaxial service providers (IntelliEPI Taiwan, Visual Photonics Epitaxy, LandMark Optoelectronics) using precursor chemicals (MOCVD trimethylgallium, ammonia, arsine; supplier base: Sumitomo Chemical, Air Liquide, specialty chemical vendors). This tier feeds optical transceiver supply and power-device foundries. Referent: epitaxial growth layer material for compound semiconductors (distinct from logic-die deposition materials already modeled).

nodes.notes: Referent: epitaxial growth layer (epi) for compound semiconductors (GaAs/InP/GaN), distinct from Si/SiO2 deposition in logic-die fabrication. Supply tightening as AI datacenter 1.6T/800G transceiver demand surges; upstream InP substrate shortage cascades to epi-layer bottleneck. MOCVD precursor supply (Sumitomo, Air Liquide, specialty chem vendors) generally available but subject to specialty-grade demand volatility. Not a current bottleneck but visibility into 2027-2028 suggests risk if datacenter optical interconnect demand maintains current trajectory.

nodes.name: 300mm silicon wafers (ultra-pure, polished) - Extended with compound feedstock context
nodes.description: This node extends the existing silicon_wafer_300mm node to contextualize the distinct supplier and supply-chain profile of compound/specialty crystal wafers vs silicon. Silicon wafer supply (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers) is fundamentally different from compound wafer supply (Wolfspeed SiC, Sumitomo InP/GaAs, WIN GaAs foundry, AXT, Freiberger) in capacity dynamics, vendor concentration, and geopolitical exposure. Referent note: this extension surfaces the compound/specialty tier as a separate feedstock layer.
nodes.notes: Referent clarification: existing silicon_wafer_300mm node models silicon feedstock exclusively. Compound/specialty crystal wafers (GaN, GaAs, InP, SiC) are modeled separately as a distinct tier (see compound_crystal_wafer_substrates node) with its own supplier base and supply-chain dynamics. Silicon oversupply 2024-2025 contrasts with SiC oversupply and InP optical shortage; these dynamics must be tracked separately per referent.

edges.claim: Logic-die fabrication does not directly require compound crystal wafers; this edge is a boundary marker documenting that compound/specialty wafer feedstock is NOT a bottleneck for silicon-logic AI accelerator modules but is a critical feedstock tier for power-delivery and optical-interconnect specialty devices in the broader AI platform ecosystem.

Power delivery substrate and control electronics for multi-hundred-watt AI accelerator modules increasingly rely on GaN/SiC power semiconductor devices (e.g., gate drivers, buck converters, voltage regulators). These devices are manufactured in specialty/compound foundries (GlobalFoundries, Samsung, DB HiTek GaN/SiC programs), distinct from silicon-logic foundry.

Thermal control electronics (e.g., optical transceiver chiplets for liquid-cooling sensor networks, power-control analog devices for cooling fans) rely on specialty analog devices from GaAs/InP foundries (WIN Semiconductors optical RF foundry, VIS) and GaN/SiC power control chiplets.

Advanced optical interconnect for 1.6T and 800G datacenter transceiver modules relies on GaAs/InP optical semiconductor foundries (WIN Semiconductors GaAs, VIS multi-substrate, Wafer Works InP pilot). This is a distinct tier from silicon-logic ASIC foundry.

GaN/SiC/GaAs/InP power and optical semiconductor foundries require their respective compound/specialty crystal wafers (SiC for power devices, InP/GaAs for optical devices). This is the critical upstream feedstock tier for specialty foundries.
GaN/SiC/GaAs/InP specialty foundries rely on epitaxial layer growth services (MOCVD, MBE) to deposit active device layers on crystal wafers. This is a critical upstream materials tier.
Wolfspeed is the leading merchant supplier of 8-inch (200mm) SiC crystal wafers for power semiconductor fabrication; transitioning from 6-inch commodity phase to 8-inch ramp 2026+.

Sumitomo Electric Industries is the global leader in InP optical wafer supply and among three major GaAs substrate suppliers (duopoly/triopoly with AXT, Freiberger). Critical supplier for optical RF device feedstock.

IntelliEPI is the leading Taiwan-based epitaxial wafer service provider for GaAs/InP/GaSb optical and RF epi-wafers using MBE technology. Elevated capacity utilization 2025-2026 due to AI optical demand surge.
WIN Semiconductors is the world's leading pure-play GaAs wafer foundry, serving ~75% of merchant GaAs foundry market. Critical for optical communications and RF device manufacturing.
Samsung Electronics GaN/SiC power foundry entered market Q2-Q3 2026 after pivoting from IDM device model. 8-inch GaN production ramp in progress; SiC samples H2 2026.
GlobalFoundries expanded GaN/SiC power foundry capability via TSMC technology license (Nov 2025) and strategic Navitas partnership; production ramp H1 2026, volume H2 2026+.

AI datacenter 1.6T/800G optical transceiver modules depend on Coherent Corp. as the primary supplier of InP-based electro-absorption modulated lasers (EMLs) and continuous-wave lasers (CW-LDS). CEO has warned InP capacity constrained through 2027-2030; NVIDIA multi-billion-dollar LTA secures capacity.
